answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes of knowing or should knowing that an accident involving a death has occurred.

claims.text: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA within 15 minutes once it knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained so that the incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the miner for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: An underground metal or nonmetal mine must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills shall be held at least once every six months to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or designated points of safety within self-rescue device time limits.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties, with approximately 8 hours of that training given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before such miner is assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 hours of this training shall be given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level (PEL) for noise is a time-weighted average over 8 hours (TWA8) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a noise dose of 100% as defined by the standard (integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA).

claims.text: Permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines (30 CFR Part 56), berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels that roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about FAA certification requirements for pilots flying drones over mine sites. These chunks only cover MSHA (Mine Safety and Health Administration) regulations regarding mine map certification by registered engineers/surveyors, certified mine foremen/examiners, and training record certification—none of which relate to FAA drone pilot certification.
